title: Terraform module for VPC internal ingress (NLB -> ALB) and TLS termination
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Deliver a reusable Terraform module that provisions an internal-only ingress layer for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will support an NLB fronting an internal ALB (pattern used for cross-subnet TCP forwarding and to enable TLS passthrough vs termination tradeoffs), or an ALB-only configuration where TLS is terminated on the ALB using ACM or customer-provided certs. The module must expose clear inputs for listener configuration, certificate ARNs, health-check policies, target group definitions, and lifecycle/upgrade knobs to allow zero-downtime replacements in production.
acceptance_criteria: Module instantiates in a customer VPC in < 10 minutes in staging with provided VPC and subnet ids
Supports two modes: 'nlb-proxy' (NLB TCP listener -> ALB target) and 'alb-terminate' (ALB HTTPS listener with TLS cert)
Health checks configurable per-target-group and default to /healthz (HTTP) or TCP passthrough where appropriate
Outputs include LB ARNs, DNS names, target group ARNs, listener ARNs, and security group IDs
Terraform plan must show no destructive changes for a routine cert rotation when 'replace_cert' flag is false
Zero-downtime upgrade path documented and validated via integration test: create new target group, wait for healthy, switch listener target, drain old targets
Smoke test suite (automated) verifies TLS handshake, HTTP 200 on /healthz, and CloudWatch metrics for healthy host counts
Module passes security review checklist: least-privilege IAM, logging enabled, encryption in transit (TLS), and KMS for private keys if provided
tasks: Design module interface: variables and outputs (inputs: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, mode, certificate_arn, listeners, target_groups, health_check configs, security_group_ids)
Implement Terraform 1.5-compatible module with provider version pinned and detailed examples
Add option for ALB-only (internal) and NLB-proxy mode with clear docs for when to use each
Implement health-check defaults and allow override per target group
Add lifecycle rules and 'create_before_destroy' patterns where safe to enable rolling replacements
Write unit tests using kitchen-terraform and integration test in ephemeral staging account
Add CI pipeline steps: terraform fmt/check, tflint, terraform plan on PR, and automated apply to staging with approval
Document migration and rollback procedures for existing internal ingress stacks
Coordinate with networking and security for SG rules and cross-account peering scenarios
notes: Tradeoffs considered: terminating TLS at ALB gives full Layer 7 routing and host-based health checks vs terminating at NLB allows TCP passthrough and lower latency for some protocols
We will not implement public-facing ALBs in this module (private-only). Public ingress will remain a separate module to avoid accidental exposure

ACM integration: when using ACM in customer account, module consumes certificate_arn. For private certs, module accepts PEM/privkey via secure SSM/KMS-backed references (not raw values in TF state) - security team to review
For NLB -> ALB pattern: NLB uses static IPs in private subnets for cross-AZ dependents; ensure ALB target group uses IP targets (ALB IPs) and we account for port mapping/health checks

Edge-case: AWS does not allow ALB as a direct target for NLB using instance targets; IP target mode recommended but requires subnet awareness and permission to register ALB addresses. Implementation will use IP target registration backed by a small controller in the Private deployment bootstrap to resolve ALB node IPs during creation. Document operational caveats. If this is unacceptable for some customers we provide an ALB-only fallback mode.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize variable schema and module UX, create initial TF skeleton and examples
Week 2: implement ALB-only listeners and HTTPS termination with ACM/cert acceptance; add healthcheck and target group logic
Week 3: implement NLB proxy mode and IP-target registration helper; write unit tests and example manifests
Week 4: CI integration, staging deploy, integration tests, and security review
Week 5: documentation, runbook, and handoff to Platform SRE for canary in a customer-like environment
migration_plan: Step 1: Deploy module in 'shadow' mode alongside current ingress with new ALB/target-groups
Step 2: Register a small percentage of traffic to new target group (canary) via Route53 weighted records internal-only
Step 3: Verify health checks and application metrics for 24 hours; run traffic pattern tests
Step 4: Incrementally shift weight and monitor; after 72 hours with no regressions, switch DNS aliases and decommission old target groups
Step 5: If rollback needed, revert Route53 weights and re-register old groups; automated rollback script included in runbook
upgrade_procedure: Cert rotation: create new listener with new cert, attach new target group, update DNS alias to new listener, then remove old listener after drain completes
LB replacement: create replacement ALB with new settings, switch target groups over using 'create_before_destroy' and update outputs
Terraform state handling: use import guidance in README and a preflight t plan step that warns on resource replace operations
Automation: CI pipeline will include a 'dry-run' smoke test against a staging cluster before any production apply
testing: Unit: tflint and terraform validate for every PR
Integration: ephemeral staging deployment in sandbox account run by CI on merge to main
E2E: TLS handshake, HTTP 200 on /healthz, deregistration/drain test, and Route53 weight shift test
Chaos test: simulate target termination and validate connection draining and SLO preservation
observability: ALB access logs to S3 with lifecycle policy
Healthcheck failures alerting (PagerDuty low-latency channel) and a dashboard in Console for per-customer ingress health
Trace hooks: option to inject X-Request-Id header at the ALB level for tracing convergence
risks: NLB->ALB IP registration complexity across accounts and subnets may be brittle; requires careful testing
ACM Private CA integration may not be available in customer accounts, requiring manual cert management
Terraform lifecycle rules (create_before_destroy) can still cause brief capacity reductions if targets take long to become healthy
Misconfiguration of security groups can accidentally expose services; defaults must be locked down
